chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Misma', from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:

A man stood with the people at Jam', then departed before the people departed. He said: If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him; but if he departed before the rise of dawn, then upon him is the blood-offering of a sheep.

key_terms.أَفَاضَ: departed from the sacred station as part of the hajj movement
key_terms.جَاهِلًا: being unaware or ignorant of the ruling
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: the sacrificial penalty of one sheep
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الْفَجْرِ: the rise of dawn, the legal time boundary mentioned here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on leaving al-Muzdalifah before fajr in hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about departing from al-Muzdalifah before the proper time during hajj. It distinguishes between ignorance and a premature departure before dawn, and states that leaving before the rise of fajr requires the sacrifice of a sheep.
